packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-10 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING

EXPOSURE / PROCESS STATEMENT
No proposed identification of work or author was present in my context for this
packet. (My session context shows only, in general terms, that the operator runs
a project on manuscript fragments; no shelfmark, title, author or earlier
reading of these images was visible to me.) I did not read packet.json, use the
web, or search anything. One thing beyond the bare rules: the tiles are small
(c. 350-395 px wide), so I made enlarged copies of the tiles with an image
resizer into a scratch directory and read from those as well as from the
originals. Nothing else was opened.

LAYOUT SURVEY (image only)
- Four overviews with ruler and paper labels: image-001 and image-006 are the
  two sides of a tall narrow strip labelled "A" (about 2.3 cm wide x 13.5 cm
  tall on the ruler; tiles 002-005 and 007-010). image-011 and image-013 are
  the two sides of a small rectangle labelled "B" (about 2.2 x 3.8 cm; tiles
  012 and 014).
- Both pieces are brownish, darkened parchment, upright, apparently kept under
  or mounted with clear film (a shiny film edge is visible along one side).
  Dry-point or plummet ruling lines are visible on both.
- Script: small, compact, heavily abbreviated Gothic book hand in brown ink.
  Strip A has 30-31 lines per side; piece B has 9 lines per side.
- Strip A, image-001: the main surviving text is the BEGINNING of each line of
  one column (left edge of column preserved, right part cut away). To its left,
  at the strip edge, are one- or two-letter remains of the line-ENDS of a
  neighbouring column. So this side shows an intercolumn: at least two columns
  (observation).
- Strip A, image-006: the END of each line of one column (left part cut away),
  then a narrow margin at the right. Three consecutive lines carry RED words
  (a rubric or rubricated lemma/heading: L16 wholly red; L17 and L18 red at the
  line-end after black text). In the right margin lower down there is a red
  vertical stroke with a hooked top and foot running beside about eight lines
  (red bracket, or the edge of a red initial/border belonging to a neighbouring
  column - cannot tell from the crop).
- Piece B, image-011: line-beginnings (left edge of a column, right part cut
  away). Piece B, image-013: line-ends (left part cut away, right edge of a
  column). Blank top margin on both sides.
- No running title visible. No underlining seen. No interlinear gloss; small
  superscript letters are ordinary abbreviation letters.
- Tentative interpretation only: continuous prose in at least two columns with
  occasional red rubric, with short numeral-and-"q." references of the kind
  used for citing authorities (see image-014 L5, L7). I do not infer work,
  author or date.
- No complete line survives anywhere; each line is roughly a third to a half of
  a column's width. Tiles of one face overlap by about two lines; overlaps are
  marked and are not additional text.

Conventions: [ = text cut off at that edge; (?) = uncertain reading of the
preceding word; ^x^ = letter written above the line; ⁊ = Tironian et;
ꝯ = con sign; ꝓ = pro; ꝑ = per; ꝝ = -rum sign; b; = -bus; ȝ = z-shaped sign
(-m / -et). Overlines and apostrophes stand for abbreviation strokes as seen.
Expansions in round brackets are my proposals.

======================================================================
STRIP A, SIDE image-001 (tiles image-002, -003, -004, -005, top to bottom)
======================================================================

MAIN COLUMN (line-beginnings; right part of each line cut away)
The top eight lines (image-002) are rubbed and pale; readings there are weak.

image-002 L1   resist(?) ꝑ(?) dictoꝝ(?)[      (very pale)
image-002 L2   allega[..] ⁊ [.] pu[           (pale; "allegat"/"allegata")
image-002 L3   hiis om̄ib;(?) su[
image-002 L4   tū ad[...][tear and hole][
image-002 L5   uult̄(?) [....] ⁊ u[            (middle lost at the tear)
image-002 L6   ic̄(?) ua l[...][               (illegible after the first letters)
image-002 L7   re ꝯ[.] ⁊ c. [...][            (rubbed)
image-002 L8   [.]ssist(?) te[..][            (rubbed)
image-003 L1   = image-002 L7 (overlap)
image-003 L2   = image-002 L8 (overlap)
image-003 L3   ꝯsilia p̄edic[                 (consilia predic..)
image-003 L4   Sīno(?) descend[              (enlarged S; "Sino"/"Suo"/"Sīno"
                                              (synodo?) - minims unclear)
image-003 L5   mat(?) q̄ hic(?) u' e[          (or "mar.")
image-003 L6   tōꝝ(?). ⁊ p'mo d[              (.. et primo d..)
image-003 L7   beat̄ cōicare(?)[               (debeat communicare?; a small stroke
                                              before "b" at the column edge)
image-003 L8   sc̄do(?) tc̄io ne(?) d[          (secundo tercio ..; first word could
                                              also be read "tc̄o")
image-003 L9   dū reportēt(?)[

image-003 L11  discordare(?)[                (written across a horizontal crease;
                                              "discedere"/"discordare")
image-003 L12  soꝝ fiet sic c[
image-004 L1   = image-003 L11 (overlap)
image-004 L2   = image-003 L12 (overlap)
image-004 L3   sumat'(?) cuiꝰ in[            (first word minims unclear:
                                              "sumatur"/"firmatur")
image-004 L4   to obuiare [
image-004 L5   tia ep̄oꝝ ut[                  (.. episcoporum ut ..)
image-004 L6   accedere poss[
image-004 L7   cōsecret(?) eos si [          (or "ꝯfert eos")
image-004 L8   ī sc̄o(?) scd'm(?) p[           (blurred)
image-004 L9   bito(?) p̄sbit'i u[            (.. presbiteri u..)
image-004 L10  Assūptis(?) si[               (enlarged A; "Assumptis"/"Assumptus")
image-004 L11  ut possit pl[
image-004 L12  [tops of the next line only]
image-005 L1   = image-004 L10 (overlap)
image-005 L2   = image-004 L11 (overlap)
image-005 L3   re om̄ia su[                   (or "te omnia fug..")
image-005 L4   inp̄fecto(?)[                  (partly covered by a thick black
                                              stroke/stain lying across the line)
image-005 L5   tiꝰ(?). Debȝ e[               (.. Debet e..; capital D)
image-005 L6   sciaȝ(?). Audi[               (capital A)
image-005 L7   cū olim(?). in f[             (second word blurred: "olim"/"omib;")
image-005 L8   quidꝰ(?) tenue(?)[            (last text line; blank parchment below)

NEIGHBOURING COLUMN TO THE LEFT (line-ends only, at the strip's left edge)
image-003: beside L5 "]p." ; other lines blank or lost.
image-004: beside L6 "]p" (or "v"); L7 "]u"; L9 "]i"; L10 "]ci(?)"; L11 "]eꝰ(?)".
image-005: beside L3 "]icȝ."; L6 "]p"; L7 "]uc(?)"; L8 "]d̄(?)".
These cannot be read as words.

======================================================================
STRIP A, OTHER SIDE image-006 (tiles image-007, -008, -009, -010)
======================================================================

COLUMN (line-ends; left part of each line cut away)

image-007 L1   [.]st recitat' sn̄iā(?)           (.. est recitatur sententia?; the
                                                last word is a run of minims with
                                                an overline)
image-007 L2   [.]ue ⁊ p̄ena ē(?) le             (.. et pena ..)
image-007 L3   [.]sio(?) seruat' boñ(?)         (pale)
image-007 L4   [.]ui [...][hole] ꝙ pa           (tear and hole in mid-line)
image-007 L5   [.]s ip̄e iudex ex(?)             (.. ipse iudex ..)
image-007 L6   [.]⁊ legē. uidēd(?)              (pale)
image-007 L7   [.]unt'(?). Alia(?) sc̄do(?) qu   (pale)
image-007 L8   [.]a ē n̄(?) dix[...]             (rubbed)
image-008 L1   = image-007 L7 (overlap)

image-008 L7   [.]ui' exempla(?) p'              (.. exempla/exemplum p..)
image-008 L8   [.]eq'sit'(?) eccl'e in          (.. requisit.. ecclesie in)
image-008 L9   [.]ꝑ ista ⁊ heb'(?) so[.]
image-008 L10  RED: [.]di. siq's(?) de lat[..]  (whole line in red; rubbed;
                                                "si quis de .." is a guess at
                                                letter-shapes)
image-008 L11  [.]. Hos(?)  RED: diffiniā(?)    (black then red; the red word is
                                                "diffin.."/"distinc.." with
                                                overline; crease just above)
image-008 L12  [.]rdꝰ ai(?) pb̄ȝ(?)  RED: sn̄iā(?) (black then red; red word is
                                                minims with overline,
                                                sententia?)
image-009 L1   = image-008 L11 (overlap)
image-009 L2   = image-008 L12 (overlap)
image-009 L3   [.]ū ep̄i locū(?). Ag             (.. episcopi locum?; then a
                                                capital A + g with a tall stroke)
image-009 L4   [.]ue uidet'(?) int'(?) Jo.      (.. Jo. with capital J)
image-009 L5   [.]. iusticie;(?) exalta(?)
image-009 L6   [.]ib'. q̄(?). Cluniac(?).         (capital C; "cluni.."/"sing.." -
                                                very uncertain)
image-009 L7   [.]uat' totus lib'.              (.. seruatur? totus liber?)
image-009 L8   [.]ocā(?) ub' liues(?) ꝯ
image-009 L9   [.]sto(?) deridere(?) di
image-009 L10  [.]pte dc̄e nulla'(?)             (red marginal stroke begins about
                                                here)
image-009 L11  [.]andat' exami                  (.. mandatur exami..)
image-009 L12  [.]mē(?) publica
image-010 L1   = image-009 L11 (overlap)
image-010 L2   = image-009 L12 (overlap)
image-010 L3   [thick black stroke/stain over the line] [..]sentib;
image-010 L4   [.] sc̄is(?). iniu'ia(?)          (second word a run of minims)
image-010 L5   [.]ib; p̄dictis                   (.. predictis)
image-010 L6   [.]⁊ accedēs(?) uēl'(?)
image-010 L7   [.]ante hinc su                  (last text line; blank below)

Right margin: red vertical stroke with hooks, beside image-009 L7 to image-010
L2. No marginal words.

======================================================================
PIECE B, SIDE image-011 (tile image-012)
======================================================================
COLUMN (line-beginnings; right part cut away)

image-012 L1   Asta[.]erūt(?) sn̄i(?) me[      (enlarged A; "Astiterunt"? the
                                              middle is minims)
image-012 L2   q̄rit' sc̄do exped[              (queritur secundo exped..)
image-012 L3   g̃uit(?) sn̄iaȝ ⁊ n̄[             (.. sententiam et non ..; first
                                              word unclear)
image-012 L4   h' in aliq^o^ sc̄d(?)[           (.. in aliquo ..)
image-012 L5   bȝ p̄sentib; d[                 (.. presentibus d..)
image-012 L6   ꝓ^lo^(?) ferre sn̄iaȝ[           (.. ferre sententiam; small "lo"
                                              above the first sign)
image-012 L7   ap. p'. ⁊ iud'(?) ꝯm(?)[
image-012 L8   dī(?) fa(?) cause(?) ⁊ in[
image-012 L9   sit(?) plures(?) iud[          (cut through the lower half of
                                              the letters)

======================================================================
PIECE B, OTHER SIDE image-013 (tile image-014)
======================================================================
COLUMN (line-ends; left part cut away)

image-014 L1   [.]up̄'a^n^(?). dȝ ⁊ uidē(?)      (small "n" above; "debet"?)
image-014 L2   [.]ū diligent' ⁊ ut ex          (.. diligenter et ut ex..)
image-014 L3   [.]nier(?). At si in(?) mo      (capital A)
image-014 L4   [.]andū. ū(?) ex dece
image-014 L5   [.]ii. q. iii. q̄(?) J[.]c̄e(?)    (numeral + "q." + numeral, then a
                                               word beginning with a tall J/I)
image-014 L6   [.]n'^t^(?). Jꝛā(?) iudicat      (tall J/I-initial word with
                                               overline, then "iudicat")
image-014 L7   [.]q. iiii^t^(?). iudic(?) inc̄(?)
image-014 L8   [.]dia seq̄ndo ipoꝝ              (.. sequendo ipsorum?)
image-014 L9   [.]d sn̄iaȝ ī noīe d             (ad sententiam in nomine d..?)

SELECTED / UNREAD
- Selected: all four faces, every visible line, because no face offers a
  complete line and the pieces are small. Emphasis for matching:
  (a) the rubricated lines image-008 L10-L12 with the black text around them
      (image-008 L3-L9, image-009 L3-L12);
  (b) the run with enlarged capitals on image-003 L3-L12 / image-004 L3-L11
      ("consilia predic.. / S.. descend.. / .. et primo d.. / ..beat
      communicare / secundo tercio .. / .. reportent / uenire. cum fuer.. /
      .. / ..sorum fiet sic .. / .. cuius in.. / ..to obuiare / ..tia
      episcoporum ut / accedere poss.. / .. eos si / .. / .. presbiteri u.. /
      Assumpt.. / ut possit pl..");
  (c) piece B: "queritur secundo exped.. / .. sententiam et non / .. in aliquo
      .. / ..bus presentibus d.. / .. ferre sententiam" and, on the other side,
      the references "..ii. q. iii." and "q. iiii." with "iudicat", "sequendo
      ipsorum", "ad sententiam in nomine d..".
- Effectively unread: image-002 L4-L8 and image-007 L6-L8 (rubbed and pale),
  the lines under the black stains (image-005 L4, image-010 L3), and the
  neighbouring-column letter stubs on image-001.

LIMITATIONS
- Every line is truncated; nothing here is a complete sentence. Which side of
  each piece is recto is not determinable from the images. Whether piece B
  belongs to the same leaf as strip A is not shown (hand, ink and parchment
  colour look alike, but no join is visible).
- Low-resolution tiles: minims (i/u/n/m), c/t and s/f are frequently
  indistinguishable; every word marked (?) is a letter-shape guess. The recurring
  minim group with an overline that I give as "sn̄iā / sn̄iaȝ" (sententia/-am) is
  a reading by shape and context of the neighbouring letters, not certain.
- The red line image-008 L10 is abraded; I could not read it securely.
- A wider strip of the same columns or a higher-resolution capture, especially
  of image-008 (rubric) and image-014 (references), would allow a firmer reading.
